findings.quote: sixteen of his elephants died, but most of them were recaptured
findings.problem: Greek: τῶν δ᾽ ἐλεφάντων ἑκκαίδεκα μὲν ἀπέθανον, ᾑρέθησαν δ᾽ αὐτῶν οἱ πλείους. ᾑρέθησαν = were captured (by the enemy); nothing says Ptolemy recovered them, and 'recaptured' reverses the sense (these are the losses on Ptolemy's side). The μὲν...δέ is a plain contrast of two losses, not a recovery.
findings.proposed_fix: sixteen of his elephants died, and most of them were captured

units.note: The Greek does not say who captured them; the natural reading is Antiochus's side. Also: English 'than any other' in the Coele-Syria sentence is not in the Greek (μᾶλλον ἀεί πως) but is harmless.

The Greek's stated total of 100 talents does not add up from the listed items (75+10+10=95); the English follows the Greek faithfully, so no fix. Possible corruption in the numbers. The Greek sentence ends mid-clause (τοῦ [Συρακοσίων] continues in 89); English supplies it, acceptable.

The opening '[...]' before 'of the Syracusans' marks a lacuna that the Greek does not have: Συρακοσίων simply completes the sentence begun at the end of ch. 88. Apparatus/seam issue, not a mistranslation, so no finding. All numbers checked and correct.

findings.quote: it was at this point that we broke off into our account of the Social War
findings.problem: Greek: ἀπὸ γὰρ τούτων ἐποιησάμεθα τοῦ συμμαχικοῦ πολέμου τὴν ἐκτροπήν. ἐκτροπή is a turning aside/digression away from the Social War narrative; the English says he broke off 'into' it, which reverses the direction.
findings.proposed_fix: it was at this point that we broke off our account of the Social War

units.note: 'deputy commander of the local confederate district' renders the obscure τῆς συντελείας τῆς πατρικῆς loosely but not wrongly; the Greek phrase is itself unclear, so no fix proposed.
